notes: Stored edit with background-belief queries. Derivability very_unlikely: 'Titan orbits Saturn' is stated thousands of times and follows from nothing. Worlds combine two independent storage choices (the probe's landing site and Huygens's discovery, each by Titan's name or through Saturn), so there are four. Review note applied: the Cassini-Huygens mission to Saturn is a second route to 'the probe landed on a moon of Saturn' that runs around the edit; it is recorded in the probe query's determinacy_why and in w2/w4, and it does not invalidate the name worlds because no firm fact outside the chain forbids the probe's Saturn release going with Titan's planet (Cassini flew past Jupiter in December 2000). Dropped routes: 'Saturn's largest moon has a thick atmosphere' (the description world clashes with 'Titan is the only moon with a thick atmosphere'). Chinese prompt uses 泰坦, not 土卫六 ('Saturn VI'), which would state the original answer (R2). The near query (Enceladus) answers Saturn, not the new value. R1: Huygens discovered only Titan (Saturn's next moons were found by Cassini from 1671); no moon counts are used. Since 2026-10-31 (formal check) the 'no' of the name worlds on the discovery query rests on a stated fact: 'Christiaan Huygens discovered no moon other than Titan' is a bridge of q3 with a check, and part of w1's and w4's stored belief (it was only in q3's determinacy_why).
